messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased OOM rate on paged-attention allocator in us-west-2 pool. 12 containers restarted in last 6m, node flaps detected. Auto-fallback to smaller model attempted for some routes.

marta: seeing the same. p99 latency up ~2x for chat endpoints. Not all requests fail but some get 502 after container restarts.

raj: confirming OOMs show CUDA driver errors right before container exit. attaching snippet:```
[pid 20456] cudaGetLastError() -> out of memory
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/attn_paged.cpp", line 442, in allocate_page
  ...
````

ellen: nv-hostdiag shows memory stalls on GPU 0/1 around the same times. nvidia-smi shows GPU mem near 100% then sudden drop as container restarts.

sam: can we rate-limit routed traffic to the affected pool and switch routing policy to dedicated smaller instances? I can flip routing at the LB if we decide.

marta: yes, start with traffic diversion. put low-priority customer routes onto fallback pool. keep high-tier on smaller model variants.

ops-bot: Routing change request queued by @sam to lb-switcher service (req id r-3521).

raj: quick mitigation note: we suspect KV cache fragmentation + tiny-page allocator drift causing slow memory creep. Eviction doesn't reclaim fragmented slabs. Repro rate increases with sequence length > 4k.

ellen: reproduced locally with long-context test harness. Patch in dev reduces allocation churn but not live.

marta: rolling a hotfix to increase aggressive_slab_eviction to 0.9 on affected nodes. can someone run the command?

sam: running sudo rctl apply --pool=us-west-2 --key=aggressive_slab_eviction --value=0.9
sam: command succeeded, applying to 8 nodes.

incident-bot: AUTO: nodes flagged for hotfix: node-72, node-73, node-74, node-75, node-76, node-77, node-78, node-79.

marta: watching metrics... p95 mem per-gpu dropped a bit on node-72/73. OOMs still happening on node-75 though.

raj: node-75 log attach:```
[2026-03-15T01:07:12Z] allocator: page_alloc failed attempt=3242 size=65536
[2026-03-15T01:07:12Z] kv_cache: stale_span_count=1423 free_spans=3 fragmented_bytes=1.9GB
[2026-03-15T01:07:12Z] runtime: cudaErrorIllegalAddress -> container restart
```

ellen: fragmented_bytes number is worrying. Looks like a slow creeping fragmentation where free spans are many but unusable due to alignment.

marta: next mitigation: quiesce long-running inference sessions on node-75 and force compact on restart. We'll cordon node-75. @lee (oncall-2) can you cordon and drain?

lee (oncall-2): cordon/evict started for node-75. Eviction mode: best-effort, background re-schedule. ETA ~90s per container.

ops-bot: cordon request accepted. node-75 -> DRAINING.

sam: switching traffic off node-75 at lb now. r-3521 updated.

marta: customer impact check: support reports a spike in 502s from a small set of customers on us-west. No-wide customer outage yet. @ellen can you prepare a short blurb for customer-facing triage?

ellen: draft: "We’re investigating intermittent 502s and latency on some inference routes in us-west-2, related to GPU memory pressure. We’ve rerouted traffic and are applying mitigations; we’ll update in 30 minutes or on conclusion."

marta: fine to post to status once we confirm reroute success.

raj: root cause hypothesis doc note (quick): "Paged-attention allocator is accumulating small residual spans when pages are re-mapped under high fragmentation; GC/compaction policy doesn't coalesce across slab classes, leading to ineffective eviction and slow OOM creep. Coupled with long-seq requests this trips CUDA memory allocation failures."

sam: quick workaround proposal: enable prefix/KV hot-cache flush on long-seq requests + force model-shard fallbacks for sequences > 4k. We should also lower max inflight tokens per session temporarily.

marta: implement workarounds now. @sam flip the token limits and fallback rules. @raj keep working on a proper compaction fix. @lee start post-mitigation soak checks.

lee (oncall-2): token limit lowered for us-west pool. fallback policy active. Starting 15-minute canary watch.

incident-bot: Note: new deploys are paused in us-west-2 until incident cleared.

raj: for the code fix we plan a compact-on-evict pass that can reclaim fragmented spans; instrumenting dev tests now. Expect PR in ~4h, but need careful perf testing.

ellen: after cordon, node-75 had no further OOMs during drain and compaction on restart freed ~2.1GB reported by agent.

marta: good. next: handoff checklist for next oncall (lee) at +30m: 1) confirm no new OOMs for 30m, 2) validate no regressions on latency > 99th, 3) coordinate with runtime team for PR review, 4) notify customer comms owner.

lee (oncall-2): taking handoff. I'll monitor and post a 30m update.

ops-bot: Handoff created: incident-3521, assigned to lee (oncall-2).

sam: escalations: pinging @raj and @marta for code review when PR is ready. Also flagging infra to consider allocation-policy audit across other regions.

ellen: posting metrics snapshot to thread: p50 p95 p99 latencies, GPU mem curves, OOM counts (attached in internal dashboard).

marta: summary for postmortem: cause: allocator fragmentation + eviction policy gap -> slow memory creep -> CUDA OOMs -> container restarts -> node flaps. Mitigations: routing diversion, aggressive eviction toggle, node cordon & compaction on restart, fallback routing + token limits. Next steps: compaction code, longer-term allocator redesign, add fragmentation alarms.

lee (oncall-2): confirming handoff. Will update at 30m or sooner if it flares.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: 10m since interventions. OOMs reduced to 1 event in last 10m (was 8). Status: stabilizing.

marta: thanks everyone. keep the thread alive for the postmortem notes.

lee (oncall-2): 30m check-in: no new OOMs for 30m, p99 improved. Marking as monitoring; prepping postmortem stub.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: monitoring -> assign postmortem tag incident-3521-paged-mosaic-drift for follow-up."
